---
title: "Section 2: Sand Flies and Leishmania"
---

This section applies the **C.R.E.A.T.E.** method to a second article. Where the first section followed *Delftia* and malaria in mosquitoes, this one follows *Delftia tsuruhatensis* TC1 and *Leishmania* in sand flies.

**Anchor article:** Cecilio, P. et al. (2025). *Leishmania* sand fly-transmission is disrupted by *Delftia tsuruhatensis* TC1 bacteria. *Nature Communications* 16:3571. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58769-4>

## How the section is organized

The section has seven two-week modules (14 weeks, one 50-minute meeting per week).

| Module | Focus | CREATE step | Signature activity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Getting started | Consider | Concept Map Showdown |
| 2 | Introduction to the article | Read | Hypothesis Board |
| 3 | Methods | Read | Methods Market and Method Card |
| 4 | Figure analysis I (Figs 1–3) | Elucidate, Analyze | Figure Detectives and Mechanism Tribunal |
| 5 | Figure analysis II (Figs 4–6) | Analyze | Field Advisory Brief, R0 Lab |
| 6 | Discussion and implications | Analyze, Think | Write the Discussion |
| 7 | Next experiment and grant proposal | Think | Mini-Grant Panel |

## Pre-class annotation tags

Annotate the article in Perusall with these text-based tags so meaning never depends on color:
`#Concept`, `#Known`, `#Gap`, `#Question`, `#Hypothesis`, `#Method`, `#Term`, `#Inference`, `#EffectSize`, `#Assumption`, `#Claim`, `#Evidence`, `#Limit`, `#MyLimit`, `#Strength`, `#Suggestion`, `#NextExperiment`.

## Group roles

Rotate these roles each module: **Facilitator**, **Recorder**, **Evidence checker**, **Reporter**.

## Group challenge rubric (12 points)

Score each row from 1 to 3.

| Criterion | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Use of evidence | Little or no data cited | Some data cited | Specific data cited and checked |
| Scientific reasoning | Claims unsupported | Partly reasoned | Claim, evidence and reasoning linked |
| Collaboration | One voice dominates | Some sharing | Roles shared and respected |
| Communication | Hard to follow | Mostly clear | Clear, concise and accurate |

## Suggested grade weights

Perusall 15%, knowledge checks 10%, group challenges 25%, portfolio 35%, Mini-Grant Panel 10%, participation 5%.

## Source reliability: four questions

1. Who wrote it?
2. Was it reviewed?
3. How recent is it?
4. What evidence does it give?

Record each source in your **source log** with a 2–3 sentence reliability note.

::: {.callout-note}

:::
